740255202.text: (Maybe we'll even be able to get some Coupons...)

740250401.text: I knew that wouldn't be the end of the problem. People like you just keep appearing, don't you? What's that idiot Clynes doing anyway — isn't he supposed to come up with solutions?

740250403.text: Alright, if you've got questions about processes or documents, I don't want to hear them. Can't fix 'em, anyway. Go look for Monglane instead. She's the one in charge of that.

740255302.text: (Maybe we'll even be able to get some Coupons...)

subQuests.subQuestName: Learn about the situation from Monglane

740250203.text: I'm a receptionist here at the Fortress of Meropide. Everyone calls me Monglane. Alright, your turn.

740250207.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon, huh... Never heard of you two. Are you really from around these parts?

740250206.text: And you can call Paimon Paimon... *cough* Gah, lowering our voices didn't make us sound more serious at all. In fact, we sound super weird!

subQuests.subQuestName: Learn about the situation from Monglane

740258301.text: What are we waiting for? Let's go!

740250801.text: Well? Want to go find Estienne with me now?

740250901.text: Hi, Estienne. I've brought two new friends with me.

740250902.text: Your new friends may have come at a bad time. See that? They're gonna be at it for a while.

740250903.text: ...That's an unscientific way of keeping score. Besides, the participants were unsupervised. Is that any way to produce convincing results? I'm calling for a reassessment.

740250904.text: This is a competition, of course we should have a refined system and fair rules. Participants who don't follow the rules should be disqualified.

740250905.text: You talk a good game. I'd expect nothing less from someone who's been through the wringer.

740250906.text: If you're referring to the fraudulent thesis case, I've already made my point several times now. The case is still under investigation. It's useless to try and attack my character with something like that.

740250907.text: If you say so. After all, you're the only one who knows the truth.

740250908.text: Oh, it's Genevieve and Rave again. I'll talk to you about my thing later then, I'm gonna bounce for now... I'll leave my two new friends to you!

740250909.text: Darcy makes a dash for it...

740250910.text: He left us, just like that? Some guide, Paimon gives him zero stars! Zero!

740250911.text: Mr. Guard, as the organizer, it's not exactly proper for you to stay out of this discussion of the rules, is it?

740250912.text: Haha, this is just a game to pass the time. How was I supposed to know you'd all get so riled up over it... let alone take it this seriously.

740250913.text: Right, why don't we introduce the rules of the game to the new players?

740250915.text: Heh, there's no game the two of us can't win! Wait a sec, we still don't know what the game even is yet...

740250918.text: Don't try and change the subject! We're already halfway through the game, and they don't even know the fundamental rules. They can't just join in now.

740250919.text: So, what are you guys playing?

740250921.text: Paimon has never heard of such a game...

740250922.text: Of course not, this is just what the heartless guards play to make fun of us. Everyone loses, and I'm sure you know who wins.

740250923.text: That's not true. You work to earn Coupons during the game, and the one that has the most Coupons will get an even better reward from me.

740250924.text: So everyone wins, but one person wins more than the rest.

740250925.text: A reward better than Coupons? What could it be?

740250926.text: In Darcy's words, a chance to be under the sun. Some of our periodic checks need to be performed outside, and I get to decide who gets these jobs.

740250927.text: It wouldn't be very interesting if I just picked based on my preference.

740250928.text: So I created Coupon Millionaire, and those who want to go outside are free to sign up. Whoever gets the most Coupons wins the game.

740250929.text: If you feel that your strength alone will be insufficient, you can find others to group up with. As for how you earn Coupons... I don't care about that.

740250930.text: As far as games go, the rules are really vague.

740250931.text: It's part of the strategy. Does the Fontaine Research Institute not have similar "games"?

740250933.text: How about you, Darcy's new friends?

740250917.text: That's right, we don't even know what this game is. If it's an eating competition, Paimon will absolutely play! But if it's some sort of game involving a lot of hard work and very little reward... then you can forget about it!

740255101.text: The entrance to the Rift of Erosion.

740255102.text: (Maybe we'll even be able to get some Coupons...)

740251404.text: It's the evil sorcerer's magic! We'll be trapped if we get caught in it!

740251405.text: Sorry, the light's broken, and this expert here isn't anywhere near as good as he claimed...

740251406.text: I never said such a thing.

740251407.text: Oh, it's you! It's alright, you're a good sorceress.

740251408.text: But that bright light really hurt my eyes...

740254201.text: Sorry for the delay. About the way I said I got the Coupons earlier...

740254202.text: What did you do to him?

740254203.text: Someone that aggressive doesn't seem like the type to take advice from anyone. Why would he give up so easily...?

740254205.text: "The culprit is where he should be." This is an undeniable fact.

740254206.text: Making someone as straightforward as him "certain" of an undeniable fact isn't exactly hard.

740254208.text: That's right. Just like that time with Julien.

740254209.text: I've been here for a long time, as you know. After staying in one place for a long time, it's only natural to pick up a few handy tricks to exert some degree of influence over your environment.

740254212.text: Changing a stubborn person's mind with just a few simple phrases almost sounds like magic... Could there have been times when we were also influenced by magic without even knowing it?

740251601.text: Phew, guess our adventure's almost at an end. The Coupon Cafeteria's our final stop.

740251602.text: So the ultimate destination of adventuring is a good meal.

740251603.text: Not bad, right? Adventures take a toll on your body, so eating afterward is a must.

740251604.text: That's right! And I've never seen someone as small as Ms. Paimon! You're even smaller than Ms. Sigewinne. You should eat more, so you can grow bigger!

740251609.text: By the way, do the two of you have any Coupons?

740251611.text: Well, that means we get no food. Oops.

740251612.text: No, don't worry! Just talk to Bran, and you'll get a yummy free meal!

740251613.text: Bran's the clockwork meka over there. It was broken, but Wolsey repaired it.

740251614.text: You only get a free meal once per day, though, and you won't know what you'll get. The best thing you can get is the Tasses Ragout.

740251615.text: Wait, you won't know what you'll get? Why can't you order what you want?

740251616.text: Wolsey says that it's meant to be both a surprise and a risk precisely 'cause it's a free meal. If you don't want any risks, then you've gotta use Coupons.

740251617.text: Will the two of you try the free meal?

740251618.text: Paimon will give it a try! Paimon is always lucky, and this stuff's free! How can free meals be bad?

740251608.text: Ugh, you're probably thinking about something rude right now, aren't you?

740255001.text: (Caterpillar probably went to get Coupons elsewhere, but he left us some clues...)

740251701.text: Phew, guess our adventure's almost at an end. The Coupon Cafeteria's our final stop.

740251702.text: So the ultimate destination of adventuring is a good meal.

740251703.text: Not bad, right? Adventures take a toll on your body, so eating afterward is a must.

740251704.text: That's right! And I've never seen someone as small as Ms. Paimon! You're even smaller than Ms. Sigewinne. You should eat more, so you can grow bigger!

740251709.text: Let's talk to Bran and see if we'll get something good!

740251710.text: Yup! It'd be nice if it was the delicious Tasses Ragout, though.

740251708.text: Ugh, you're probably thinking about something rude right now, aren't you?

subQuests.subQuestName: Eat at the Coupon Cafeteria with Lanoire

740251802.text: Greetings. What can I do for you?

740251822.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, let's open our meals together, alright? Three... Two... One!

740251809.text: Negative. According to the "Fortress of Meropide's Coupon Cafeteria Regulations," only one free meal per day shall be permitted per person.

740251810.text: I'm getting one for Paimon, too.

740251811.text: That's right, don't forget about Paimon!

740251815.text: Negative. According to the "Fortress of Meropide's Coupon Cafeteria Regulations," only one free meal per day shall be permitted per person.

740251817.text: Are you seriously trying to feed everyone here? We just need two!

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Rag and Bone Shop with Lanoire

740252102.text: Hey, Skylark, want a Fonta? We just got a new shipment. How about your friends?

740252103.text: So this is the Rag and Bone Shop.

740252104.text: If you have Coupons, we have everything from home supplies like Hydro Phantasm Taint-B-Gone...

740252105.text: ...To devices that can help you in the Pankration Ring. Our wares are trusted and loved by all and sundry! You name it, Rag and Bone Shop has it!

740252107.text: We don't really need this, do we?

740252110.text: The special items must be pre-ordered, though. Or if you're lucky enough, you might find what you want on the for-sale list.

740252111.text: We do have the other stuff stocked at all times. So, back to my question. How about some Fonta?

740252112.text: Hm, I want everything in Uncle Alvard's store.

740252113.text: That's not going to be a problem. Let's see... We're almost through with this shipment, and only food and drinks are left. But they'll cost you a good number of Coupons.

740252114.text: Really!? Are you sure it won't be a problem?

740252115.text: Problem? If you mean Coupons, Cater gave me a ton of them, so I should have enough. The food and drinks here are really great, and you're going to love them, Ms. Paimon!

740252116.text: Cater said that Coupons make unfair things fair. Only I got the delicious Tasses Ragout at the Coupon Cafeteria, and that was unfair.

740252117.text: So now I'm going to use my Coupons to buy something delicious for the two of you!

740252109.text: They're for regulars only. Or, if you happen to have friends who are our regulars, I suppose I can show them to you...

740252202.text: Welcome back, Lanoire. Looks like you've made some friends.

740252203.text: #Yes, they're {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon. Ms. Paimon is small and she can fly, but she's not a bird.

740252204.text: She's not a Seelie either. Maybe a small Oceanid? No wonder no one has seen anything like her, or knows anything about her!

740252206.text: That's right, Paimon's just Paimon! She's not a Seelie or an Oceanid... Wait, you're "Cater"!?

740252207.text: You look about the same age as Lanoire.

740252208.text: #Nice to meet you, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon. Please call me Caterpillar.

740252209.text: Uh... Please don't be so formal. That feels so strange!

740252210.text: Since you're Lanoire's friends, sure, I can do that!

740252211.text: Wait a minute... We've heard the name "Caterpillar" before, haven't we?

740252214.text: Ah, that's right! Julien! The painter we met at Samudra Coast. Do you remember him? So you're the "Caterpillar" he mentioned!

740252215.text: You've met Julien? He really went to Sumeru, huh? How is he?

740252217.text: You tell him about your meeting with Julien in Sumeru...

740252218.text: According to Julien, his ability to "paint everything exactly as he sees it" came from you. Did you really give him that power?

740252219.text: Is that really what he said? I can't decide if he was exaggerating...

740252220.text: Wait, so he was lying? But the painting he made for Pepper looked so real, even though the color was a bit off.

740252221.text: That was an ability he already had. What I did was to give him "certainty." The purer the person, the more obvious the effect of such support is.

740252222.text: Pure, huh... Well, he did look kind of gullible.

740258702.text:
"Cater, what story are you gonna tell me today? I've already heard a lot of stories with heroes as the main characters..."
"Today I'll tell you a story about a little girl, then."
"A little girl... Can a little girl also be the main character?"
"Of course she can. It's her own story, after all. In other stories, she might be a hero herself, or even an evil dragon. There are all kinds of roles she can play."

740258703.text: Long, long ago, there was a little girl who lived in a giant's garden.\nThe giant took special care of the flowers in the garden, and wouldn't allow anyone to pluck even a single one of them. To keep intruders out, the giant built a towering wall around it.\nBecause of this, the little girl living in the giant's garden had never set foot outside of it even once. The giant always told her that the world outside was a dangerous place, and that the garden was the safest place she could live in.

740258704.text:
"And then what? Did the little girl listen to the giant? I bet she didn't. If she did, then the story would end there!"
"You're right. The little girl never was one for doing what she was told."
"Uh-huh...?"
"As for the rest of the story, well, let's save that for next time."

740252402.text: Welcome back, Lanoire. Looks like you've made some friends.

740252403.text: #Yes, they're {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon. Ms. Paimon is small and she can fly, but she's not a bird.

740252404.text: She's not a Seelie either. Maybe a small Oceanid? No wonder no one has seen anything like her, or knows anything about her!

740252406.text: That's right, Paimon's just Paimon! She's not a Seelie or an Oceanid... Wait, you're "Cater"!?

740252407.text: You look about the same age as Lanoire.

740252409.text: Uh... Please don't be so formal. That feels so strange!

740252410.text: Well, if you're Lanoire's friends, sure!

740252411.text: Anyway, both you and Lanoire are children, right? So, is your guardian here? Why are the two of you in a place like this...

740252413.text: Indeed, I am not. As for my present appearance... You can think of it as an illness of sorts.

740252415.text: I've been here for a long time, well, because of what I've done in the past. But it's more complicated for Lanoire...

740252418.text: You're a strange one, Ms. Paimon. I've already told you that I've always been here, haven't I?

740252419.text: Agnes, her mother, was plagued by a chronic illness and passed away some time ago.

740252420.text: I don't stick my nose into other people's lives, so I didn't know about their situation. But regardless, Lanoire wound up with no one to care for her.

740252421.text: Maybe it's because I've been here for a long time, and she's closer to me, but either way, Estienne's asked me to look after her.

740252422.text: So that's how it is... But she shouldn't be here, right? It's not like she's done anything wrong...

740252423.text: You're right. I'm just looking after her for now, and she really should be with her family.

740252424.text: And fortunately, she does indeed have family outside the Fortress.

740252425.text: So that's what she meant when she said she has a home that she doesn't know about. Will she be able to reunite with them soon?

740252426.text: About that... Things are a little complicated, and I'm afraid it won't happen all that soon.

740252428.text: Because she doesn't have any proof of identity. Maybe Agnes didn't think of that, either. She was the one who'd have needed to start the process to send Lanoire away from the Fortress.

740252429.text: How about her other family members?

740252430.text: Estienne said that Agnes wrote them in the past, but that she never received a reply and thus stopped trying altogether. If they knew about the current situation, they might change their minds.

740252431.text: That's why I want to take her to her family. And if they don't want to take her in, we'll figure something else out then.

740252432.text: Why can't I stay here? Sure, there's an evil sorcerer, but there's a good sorcerer, and you're here too! I don't want to leave.

740252433.text: Mother never came back after leaving the Fortress.

740252434.text: If I leave, does that mean that I'll never come back, just like my mother? And I'd never see you again either, Cater!

740252436.text: (I don't think Lanoire can comprehend what happened.)

740252438.text: Either way, this is no place for a child to grow up. How will a sprout bloom without sunlight?

740252439.text: You should get out of this place, Lanoire. You've heard all the stories already. There's a real world outside and a family that you are connected to.

740252440.text: I'll go with you, so you needn't be afraid.

740252441.text: I believe you. You've never lied to me.

740252442.text: But how will you get her out without proof of identity? Is there anything we can do to help?

740252443.text: Is there some loophole or a backdoor we can use?

740252444.text: There are options, but they're too risky. How about this, then? Let's follow the rules... albeit not that strictly.

740252446.text: Every so often, Estienne will bring a few people with him to do some work outside. We use this chance to get Lanoire back to her family.

740252447.text: She doesn't have any proof of identification to begin with... and the disappearance of someone who never existed on paper isn't exactly going to make news here in the Fortress.

740252448.text: You aren't talking about "Coupon Millionaire," are you? Paimon remembers Estienne saying that whoever gets the most Coupons within a time limit will win the chance to go outside...

740252449.text: Whoops. Our Coupons went straight to our stomachs.

740252450.text: Ah! And Lanoire spent a ton more cleaning the Rag and Bone Shop out! We're sure to lose now! What are we gonna do?

740252451.text: We won't lose. If Cater says we'll win, we'll definitely win.

740252452.text: Lanoire... Paimon suspects you aren't grasping the gravity of the situation at all!

740252454.text: As the transaction already took place, I'm afraid that won't be so easy.

740252456.text: It's fine. The Coupons I gave to Lanoire were for her to use as she pleased. This little mishap won't change the outcome.

740252457.text: Paimon still feels kinda bad though. Why don't we help you? Paimon remembers Estienne saying that you can play the game as a group.

740252458.text: #Really, Ms. Paimon? You and {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} will play the game with us, too?

740252501.text: Oh, it seems like we've come at a bad time...

740252506.text: #If I'm not mistaken, you must be... {NICKNAME} and Paimon? I'll come back to your question in a moment.

740252507.text: I consulted the records from the last hundred years, and I couldn't find any record of a "Caterpillar." In light of this possible mislaying of documents, we'll need your cooperation to recreate them.

740252508.text: There's nothing pressing about the matter, if you ask me. What's the rush about?

740252509.text: Estienne, I often get the impression that you couldn't care less about restoring order to this place.

740252510.text: I can't agree with your viewpoint. People who habitually indulge their every whim just can't see that too much freedom actually does them harm.

740252511.text: I'll restore order to this chaos using my own methods. I'll advise you again not to stand in the way of my work.

740252512.text: "Chaos"? Isn't that just another word for "thinking on your feet"? *sigh* You know what? Forget it.

740252513.text: Is Caterpillar your real name? Additionally, I'll need you to state your crime in as much detail as possible — the time, location, as well as the final sentence pronounced.

740252514.text: The more details you provide, the greater the likelihood we'll have of retrieving your records. If your file was indeed lost, we can fill in a portion of your records based on your statement.

740252515.text: I've been called Caterpillar for as long as I can remember. I think this name suits me best, and it's the closest thing I have to a real name.

740252516.text: Real name... Caterpillar. Confirmed to be correct. Next, state your crime.

740252517.text: I carried out a certain task under my master's orders. I failed, but some people suffered because of it nonetheless. This was my crime.

740252518.text: Your master? I'll need their full name. Also, when did this occur?

740252519.text: Unlike me, he has many names. This happened a long time ago.

740252521.text: Everything I've said is the truth.

740252522.text: His voice sounds too low to be that of a child.\n"I apologize. Were you looking for a more dramatic account? Or for some lurid details to ignite your imagination?"

740252523.text: "As for what happened that day, I could recount it sparing no detail — from the furnishings of that clandestine hall to the thoughts of my companion, which I've ventured to speculate on."

740252524.text: "But that's all just a fabrication of the mind made after the fact. We both know that's not what you're really after, for these are nothing more than stories masquerading as the truth. The real story has already turned to smoke along with that barren garden."

740252525.text: "What you want to know is a purer truth. The truth is that the culprit is where he should be. The other minutiae and trivialities are of no significance to you."\n"They're inconsequential, and thus won't shake up your order in the slightest."

740252526.text: "There's nothing here for you to trouble yourself with. Everything is as it should be."

740252527.text: The culprit is where he should be...

740252528.text: There's nothing here for me to trouble myself with. Everything is as it should be...

740252529.text: Compared to the "temporarily" missing file, surely the misuse of the Rochelle Loudspeaker is a more obvious problem.

740252530.text: Apart from the unauthorized use, we've also received a number of complaints recently of nervous breakdowns caused by its repeated use...

740252531.text: You're right, Estienne. The guards have an even greater duty to put a stop to this sort of rule-breaking. We should investigate the matter immediately.

740252532.text: What are we waiting for, then? Let's get this show on the road.

740252533.text: (That's odd. Why did he flip at the drop of a hat?)

740252535.text: Could it have something to do with that stuff Caterpillar said? Paimon just felt a little sleepy when she heard it...

subQuests.subQuestName: Meet back at the usual place

740252701.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, we've fallen way behind!

740252702.text: It's true. I've gone to ask Estienne about the current situation, and this seems to be the case.

740252703.text: Let Paimon see... Ooh! Looks like you got some Coupons too, Caterpillar! Wait, aren't we still dead last?

740252704.text: Even Darcy's ahead of us! He entered the competition by himself, didn't he? How can this be happening...

740252705.text: Because he helped the guards take care of no small number of nuisances. For example, Ms. Monglane often asks him for help.

740252706.text: Paimon sees... Wait a minute, does that mean he was so nice to us at the start because he could gain something from it...?

740252707.text: Also, won't we lose for sure if this keeps up? Urgh, if only Paimon hadn't eaten so much at the Rag and Bone Shop earlier...

740252708.text: No matter. All that counts is the total number of Coupons collected within the time limit. Using Coupons you already have doesn't affect the total count.

740252709.text: That means you can eat even more, Ms. Paimon!

740252710.text: Lanoire... Our problem right now is that we're about to lose the competition! Aren't you guys the least bit worried?

740252711.text: There's still plenty of time left before the end. We'll make it.

740252713.text: #Are you tired, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}? Let me rub your shoulders!

740252714.text: That's playing favorites, Lanoire! Paimon's tired, too!

740252715.text: Okay, then I'll rub your shoulders, too.

740252721.text: Tomorrow, we divide and conquer. We'll reconvene here once we make some gains. Sound good? We'll make better time this way.

740252722.text: Indeed... That sounds like a better plan.

740252723.text: Also, if you don't mind, we can rest here, just like before.

740252724.text: #Sure. {NICKNAME}, you can take a break now if you're tired.

740252718.text: That does like your typical motivational story, sure... But can we really pull it off?

740252719.text: You have to believe in yourself more, Ms. Paimon! The heroes of the story are all sure of themselves. That's why they're the main characters.

740252720.text: Hmm... You're right, Lanoire! We're gonna win this thing!

740258802.text: "Cater, tell me more of the story about the little girl!"\n"Last time, we left off with the little girl living in the giant's garden..."\n"I bet she leaves the giant's garden! But how does she get out of there...?"

740258803.text:
One day, the little girl heard the sound of a woman's voice coming from beyond the towering wall.
Kind-hearted giant, I am in need of the little purple flowers from your garden. Would you please give me some?
The giant refused, of course, and furiously bellowed at the woman on the other side of the garden wall to leave at once.
But the woman did not leave, and from a short distance away, she lamented that she had journeyed from afar for the little purple flowers in the garden, which she needed to cure a sick friend's illness.
Hearing the woman's plight, the little girl felt sorry for her and her friend. The giant had so many flowers in his garden. Surely having one or two less wouldn't hurt?

740258804.text: Thus, the little girl approached the garden wall and whispered to the woman that she was willing to bring the woman a few of the little purple flowers. Except, the little girl said, the giant wouldn't let her leave, and the garden's walls were so tall that she wasn't sure how she would be able to get the flowers to her from inside.\nFrom the other side of the wall, the woman told the little girl that she was actually a witch that knew many magic spells, and if the little girl could bring her the flowers she needed from the giant's garden, she could use her magic to help the little girl leave that garden...

740258805.text: "Did the little girl decide to help the witch? Hmm... I bet she did. Otherwise, the witch wouldn't be able to cure her friend's illness, right? But... But the giant said she couldn't leave the garden. If she left, wouldn't she get punished somehow?"\n"It's getting late. Let's leave that part of the story for next time."

subQuests.subQuestName: Meet back at the usual place

740253101.text: Having fun playing house with the kids?

740253108.text: Did you need us for something? We're rivals, you know. Did you really come to see if we're having a good time?

740253109.text: I have many qualities, and one that has benefited me greatly is my curiosity.

740253110.text: I always want to get to the bottom of things I don't understand, so I tend to know the facts better than others.

740253105.text: Looks like Estienne really should hold a children's version.

subQuests.subQuestName: Meet back at the usual place

740253202.text: We brought quite the haul back today. Our current standing should be...

740253203.text: Dang it! We only just pulled ahead of Darcy...

740253204.text: That's great! We're not in last place anymore!

740253205.text: But there are four of us...

740253208.text: But are we really gonna be okay like this? We still have two big hurdles ahead of us...

740253210.text: You promised me we'd win for sure, right, Cater?

740253211.text: That's right. So, don't worry too much, you two. I know that may sound strange, but...

740253212.text: Sometimes forgetting about the outcome and enjoying the fun to be had in the process isn't a bad way to go.

740253214.text: Ooh, speaking of that, Caterpillar, we received an invitation from the guy who was in first place earlier. But he was super rude, and he said that... you're a...

740253215.text: Um... Anyway, it wasn't very nice of him!

740253217.text: Just a few minor differences of opinion. He invited me to join him as well, but having no real reason to accept, I declined his offer.

740253218.text: Later, he tried to get some of his lackeys to teach me a lesson... It's true, I am a monster — the kind people like him would do well not to provoke.

740253219.text: D—Don't say that! Surely you didn't end up this way because you wanted to, right, Caterpillar?

740253220.text: If Cater is a monster, then he's one of the good ones! Just like how there are good sorcerers and bad sorcerers... *yawn*

740253221.text: What's the matter? Are you sleepy, Lanoire?

740253222.text: Mm-hmm... But I haven't heard the rest of yesterday's story yet...

740253223.text: If you're tired, you should go for an early night.

740253224.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon... Will we still meet again tomorrow?

740253225.text: Why are you asking that all of a sudden?

740253226.text: If... If you don't want to be on the same team as us anymore...

740253227.text: What are you talking about? Didn't we say we'd get first place together? There are still two more teams ahead of us, so we have to make tomorrow count!

740253228.text: #Yeah, you're right! *yawn* I'm so sleepy. Let's do our best tomorrow... Sweet dreams, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, sweet dreams, Ms. Paimon...

740258902.text: "Where we last left off, the witch told the little girl that she would use her magic to help her leave the giant's garden if the little girl brought her the little purple flowers she needed."\n"I'm really sleepy, but I want to know what happens next. What did the little girl do? Does the witch cure her friend in the end?"

740258903.text: Although the giant had warned the little girl of the many dangers of the world beyond the garden wall, the little girl had never seen what the outside world was like, so she didn't know what "danger" even was.\nShe told the voice on the other side of the wall that she would help bring her some of the little purple flowers. So many identical flowers were growing in the garden, and each looked as beautiful as the next. She didn't know why the giant treasured each and every one of them so.\nThe little girl heard laughter from the other side of the wall. Later, with a bouquet of flowers in her hands, the little girl rode a gust of wind over the wall to the world outside.

740258904.text: The tall witch took the little purple flowers from the little girl's hands. The little girl, thinking she had done a good deed, was very pleased with herself. But when she tried to return to the garden, she discovered that the wall, the garden, and the giant were no longer there.\n"Good witch, I'd like to return to the giant's garden now. Could you please use your magic to take me back?" The little girl asked.\n"But what can you give me in exchange now?" The witch replied.

740258905.text: "Huh? Then the little girl couldn't go back? I'm glad the witch could save her friend, but... I don't like this story..."\n"Everyone has stories that they don't like."\n"Then I'll tell you a story next time, Cater... I have to sleep now..."

subQuests.subQuestName: Meet back at the usual place

740253603.text: Paimon's getting deja vu... Did you need us for something?

740253605.text: Alright. I'm hoping you'll join us in launching a protest against Estienne.

740253607.text: Since you're taking part in this game as well, I think you'll understand my position. The rules should be more open and transparent...

740253609.text: The competition should restart with the new rules in place.

740253610.text: What!? Wouldn't that make all the hard work we've done so far be for nothing?

740253611.text: What's so crazy about that? It happens all the time in academia — you realize that there's an error in your thesis or methodology, and it completely invalidates the conclusion you arrived at after years of research.

740253612.text: Pretty sure that's nothing like this...

subQuests.subQuestName: Meet back at the usual place

740253702.text: Just who I was looking for.

740253704.text: Hang on. I'd like you to answer a few questions first.

740253707.text: As you probably know, the missing records need to be recreated. This isn't necessarily bad news for him, but without those records, he won't be able to leave this place even if he has legally redeemed himself.

740253708.text: As such, I hope you can answer my questions honestly.

740253709.text: Do you know when Caterpillar arrived in the Fortress of Meropide?

740253710.text: Um... He just said that he came here a long time ago, so we don't know when exactly...

740253711.text: Then I don't suppose you know the specifics of his sentence or crime?

740253713.text: Do you know anything about this "master" he mentioned earlier?

740253714.text: Paimon doesn't remember Caterpillar mentioning him before...

740253715.text: Have either of you observed anything peculiar happen while speaking to him?

740253706.text: The investigation is ongoing, so I can't disclose any specifics to you. However, I'd like you to answer a few of my questions.

740259002.text: "It's my turn to tell a story! I've heard enough stories to tell one of my own now."\n"Alright, you can be the storyteller this time."\n"Okay. My story will also begin in the giant's garden..."

740259003.text:
Long, long ago, in a garden full of purple flowers, there lived a prince, a princess, and a brave hero... Oh! And the ruler of the garden — a giant with a nasty temper.
What the witch wanted more than anything were some of the purple flowers, but the mean giant treasured them so much that he wouldn't let anyone pick even a single one.
"Kind-hearted Mr. Giant," the witch asked, "I am in need of the little purple flowers from your garden. You have so many already, could you please share just one with me?"
But the mean giant refused. "Every flower in my garden belongs to me," the giant shouted, "I won't share them with anyone!"

740259004.text: "Kind-hearted Mr. Giant," the witch continued, "please hear my tale. I traveled here from a fountain in a far-off, distant land. An Oceanid there has fallen ill, and the scent of those purple flowers brings her comfort. If you could give me just one of them, perhaps her condition will improve..."\nBut the giant, who didn't have an ounce of compassion in his heart, callously refused the witch's request. What did an Oceanid in a faraway land have to do with him?

740259005.text: "Then," the witch asked, "is there anything I can do for you? I know many magic spells, and I could use my magic to help you with someone in exchange. Will you agree to my request, kind-hearted Mr. Giant?"\nThe giant thought it over, then said that he had lost something very important to him. If the witch could use her magic to help him find it...

740259006.text: "So, they made a deal?"\n"Yep! In the end, the witch's friend recovered and the giant found what he had lost. Isn't that a better story? At least in this story, everyone gets a happy ending..."

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Administrative Area Bulletin Board

740254101.text: Strange, Caterpillar and Lanoire aren't here yet.

740254102.text: Why bother coming when you know you're going to lose?

740254103.text: I wouldn't be so certain of that.

740254104.text: That's right! You're only ahead of us by a little...

740254106.text: Can the results be announced now, Estienne? Actually, no... Let's wait a little. After all, the best must be saved for last.

740254107.text: Looks like we don't have to wait long. Here they come.

740254108.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}! Ms. Paimon! Have you seen the results yet? Did we win?

740254110.text: Well, seems everyone's here. Would you announce the results now, Estienne?

740254111.text: Of course. Oh, but the results on Caterpillar's end still need to be calculated...

740254112.text: My, my, what a cruel guard, toying with us from start to finish like that.

740254113.text: Why don't you wring out the last bit of mercy in your heart and let them know that the gap between us is too wide to cross? Stop torturing us with false hope.

740254114.text: These aren't the final results, but...

740254115.text: We should be able to win once we add the Coupons that Cater got today, right?

740254116.text: Hold on, why have Genevieve's team's points been cleared out?

740254117.text: I was against it. But this is the more logical approach with respect to the results.

740254118.text: What's that supposed to mean...? Whoa, Rave's team has so many points!

740254119.text: He doesn't need the chance to leave, and we don't need to place first.

740254120.text: You mean you gave all your Coupons to Rave? Isn't that against the rules?

740254121.text: There's no rule forbidding it. I was originally in favor of amending the rules to ensure fair play, but no one else seemed to be in support of that.

740254122.text: Indeed, there isn't a rule forbidding that. *sigh* This competition would have been far more exciting if everyone could have fully used the rules to their advantage.

740254123.text: More exciting for you, maybe. Rules don't mean a thing in a game as boring as this one. At the end of the day, it's a question of upholding one's honor.

740254124.text: Alright, now that the scores have been announced, isn't it time for the final results?

740254125.text: Our points from today haven't been added yet.

740254126.text: Hmph... A drop in the ocean.

740254127.text: Now that everything's been added, here's what the results look like.

740254128.text: #Yes! {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, look! Look! We won!

740254129.text: What...? That's impossible! What did you do?

740254130.text: Whoa... that many? Paimon's lost count... Hmm...

740254131.text: It's a trick even simpler than magic.

740254132.text: I used the Coupons I'd saved up in the past to hire a bunch of people to help me work. What we have now is the product of their work this whole time. And I believe this falls within the rules, too.

740254133.text: Even if it does, that's an insane amount...

740254134.text: I also have my reasons for needing to win, and I'd even gotten help from my two friends. It would be a real shame if we lost now.

740254138.text: #Since everything's been tallied, it's time to announce the final results. The winners of this game are Caterpillar, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, and Ms. Paimon.

740254140.text: There's nothing I can say, except that it looks like I picked a fight with the wrong opponent. I ended up in here last time for striking someone in anger. I won't make the same mistake this time.

740254141.text: ...You'll pay the price for the choices you made.

740254142.text: Whoa, Paimon didn't expect to hear someone actually say that.

740250001.text: You have remained inside the light's detection range for too long. The Fortress of Meropide's guards have detained you for being suspicious.

740250006.text: You are taken to the reception area...

740250501.text: How about it? Wanna go look for Estienne together with me?

740250601.text: Newcomers? And two of you, to boot? Welcome! Welcome to the Fortress of Meropide! I'm Darcy. Outside, they call me "Pretty Face," but that's just not cool, if you know what I mean!

740250602.text: That's what you were thinking too, right? That's why I decided to give myself a new, super cool nickname! I'm called Dirty Face now! What do you think? Pretty sick, right?

740250606.text: More importantly, we have some questions...

740250607.text: Ooh, of course! It's perfectly normal for newcomers to not know what's going on. Dirty Face Darcy, at your service!

740250605.text: It is a generally recognized title, after all. Just thinking about it fills Paimon with courage.

740250701.text: #Hello, {M#sir}{F#ma'am}, and hello to your cute companion! Dirty Face Darcy, at your service!

740250703.text: That's right, just call me Dirty Face Darcy. They used to call me Pretty Face on the outside... but that nickname is just so lame!

740250704.text: Please, just call me Dirty Face instead... Oh, that's just a cool nickname, I wash my face every day. You don't have to stand all the way over there...

740250708.text: Too bad it's not time for Pankration yet... Let me think.

740250709.text: How about this, why don't I take you to have some fun? A few folks have locked horns over the chance to go outside. I had no idea those Fontaine Research Institute guys could dish it out like that...

740250710.text: I'm guessing they'll be here any minute now... What do you think? Think of it as an opening act before the real Pankration match starts. Wanna check it out?

740250707.text: #{NICKNAME}, where'd you learn to talk like that? Don't tell Paimon... Don't tell Paimon you've picked up some bad habits... No way! Paimon won't allow it!

740251002.text: Oh, you again. And your, uh... Are you a bird, little one?

740251003.text: A bird? Paimon doesn't look like a bird...

740251007.text: That's so strange. You can fly, but you're not a bird. Are you an evil dragon? Or an evil dragonling?

740252301.text: I'm feeling a little tired. Should we rest now?

740254301.text: Sorry for the delay. About the way I said I got the Coupons earlier...

740254302.text: What did you do to him?

740254303.text: Someone that aggressive doesn't seem like the type to take advice from anyone. Why would he give up so easily...?

740254305.text: "The culprit is where he should be." This is an undeniable fact.

740254306.text: Making someone as straightforward as him "certain" of an undeniable fact isn't exactly hard.

740254307.text: The purer a person is, the more easily they tend to be influenced by others' words.

740254308.text: I've been here for a long time, as you know. After staying in one place for a long time, it's only natural to pick up a few handy tricks to exert some degree of influence over your environment.

740254311.text: Changing a stubborn person's mind with just a few simple phrases almost sounds like magic... Could there have been times when we were also influenced by magic without even knowing it?

740255401.text: The north side of the production zone's lower levels.

740255402.text: (Maybe we'll even be able to get some Coupons...)

740255501.text: The south side of the dormitory block.

740255502.text: (Maybe we'll even be able to get some Coupons...)

740255601.text: The southeast side of the production zone's upper level.

740255602.text: (Maybe we'll even be able to get some Coupons...)

740255701.text: (Looks like Caterpillar left us a few Coupon breadcrumbs to follow...)

740256001.text: Dirty Face Darcy, at your service!

740256002.text: At whose service? And when? You ran off and left us behind back there!

740256003.text: I had to. Once that researcher starts talking, there's no end to it! It was fun the first time, but I've seen it too many times already.

740256004.text: That was your first time, right? Was it fun?

740256006.text: Paimon didn't get the point, either.

740256009.text: Too bad the time for Pankration hasn't arrived yet. I think that's more fun! Anyway, we'll just have to wait.

740256101.text: Come find me if you change your mind. We're already midway through the game though, so joining now means getting a late start. Still, that would make the game more interesting, wouldn't it?

740256201.text: I told you it's a waste of time to talk to them about these things. They just don't care.

740256202.text: You know we're not that kind of people. I can't reach conclusions intuitively like you. I have to do it before making a decision.

740256301.text: Did you need me for something?

740256303.text: The smiling ones are the ones you've really got to watch out for.

740256309.text: ...You kids oughta head home. If you still have a home to go back to, that is.

740256305.text: #{M#You're not going to try to get that woman to listen to reason, are you?}{F#You seem to have more sense than her.}

740256307.text: I've got nothing to say about him.

740256403.text: You're not the boss? Why didn't you say so?

740256405.text: You don't? Then I called you "boss" for nothing. What a waste.

740256601.text: Welcome to the Rag and Bone Shop! We have everything... Oops, we don't have anything right now.

740256604.text: We'll get a new shipment soon. Don't forget to come back!

740256701.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, Ms. Paimon, and I tried a really wonderful-tasting Fonta... Ms. Paimon drank a whole lot of it, but she didn't drop down at all!

740256702.text: She must know a lot of powerful magic, then.

740256801.text: I was chatting with Ms. Monglane... She said that Natlan's nothing like Fontaine, and that she really wants to take a dip in a volcanic hot spring.

740256802.text: A volcano... Is that a flaming mountain? And mountains are... suuuuper tall mounds of rock and dirt, right? Hmm...

740256803.text: You'll get to see all these things for yourself after you leave this place, whether it's volcanos, or anything else.

740256804.text: #Then let's explore those places together, Cater! Hmm... Let's invite {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME} and Ms. Paimon, too. They'll definitely like that!

740256902.text: In that case, go get some rest.

740256903.text: Okay... But I haven't heard the rest of the story yet. I'll rest after I hear the ending...

740257001.text: The candy Ms. Galvana gave me... is so sweet.

740257002.text: Remember to brush your teeth before bed.

740257101.text: Tired from playing with those kids? You can spar with me after you've rested!

740257103.text: The stronger the opponent, the better!

740257105.text: Huh? How does the saying go again... "There's no substitute for the real thing"! Sparing with an actual person always beats punching dummies, don't you think?

740257201.text: Will it take this long? You...

740257202.text: I want to be free of these bothersome affairs, too! Really, can you just... please use the devices according to the instructions?

740257301.text: Did you need me for something?

740257303.text: #{M#Indeed, we only get the occasional bit of rainfall each year.}{F#You're a funny one, miss.}

740257401.text: Hey, do you think there will still be any pay-off in joining now?

740257402.text: This Fonta's too strong. There are quite a few flavors, though...

740257403.text: I think the health drink that guy from Sumeru is working on has some promise. Maybe I should invest a little in it...

740257404.text: I may not be your friend, but I'd advise against that.

740257502.text: ...Sorry, I have some things I need to think about.

740257601.text: What, you lost your cat, too?

740257603.text: Oh, you don't know yet? Never mind.

740257604.text: I don't think anyone here loses cats.

740257705.text: Mental labor is still labor, isn't it? But the scary thing is that, as an imperceptible form of labor, there's no way to determine its value.

740257801.text: After careful consideration, I've decided to invest in him.

740257802.text: Lasting health is more important than a fleeting moment of pleasure or mental renewal, isn't it?

740257803.text: Everyone's smart enough to understand this, I'm sure.

740257804.text: I think this idea is going places!

740257805.text: I'd advise you against asking for my opinion next time.

740257901.text: ...There's no way we need that many technicians.

740257903.text: Oh, nothing. I was just lamenting how many familiar faces from the Fontaine Research Institute are here.

740258001.text: You shouldn't have turned down my offer.

740258003.text: I hope you'll be able to stick to your convictions until the end then.

740258005.text: Opportunities like that only come around once. That's something you should understand.

740258101.text: ...We'll need additional investment to expand production.

740258102.text: It's just that Mora's been a bit tight lately. Do you think you could...

740258103.text: Nope, don't look at me. I've got nothing.

740258104.text: Don't say that! We're in this together. How about this? When we make a profit, I'll double your share.

740258201.text: Guess I only have myself to rely on in the end.

740258203.text: Humans are lonely creatures, don't you think?

740258205.text: I tried to rely on others, and it didn't work out.

740258206.text: I suppose that's to be expected. Good thing I always have a Plan B, so I'm not completely out of options.

740258401.text: I can't keep up... Let me think.

740258402.text: You're going too fast, let us think about this a little...

740258403.text: Oh, sorry! I didn't mean to make you come with me. Take your time, and come find me when you make a decision!

740258602.text: Just think of it as killing time. Anyway, come find me when you make a decision, and I'll take you to meet Estienne, my guard partner!

740259101.text: There's something else I want to ask about.

740259201.text: Let me think about it first.

740259401.text: I need a little more time.

740259602.text: Hmm... Then... Then I'll wait for you two here! Don't worry, I'm very patient!

740680101.text: "Ah! Why you... You she-devil! I remember now, I remember..."

740680102.text: No no! You must face the audience when delivering the line, with 30% regret, 60% disgust, and 40% appreciation for having survived a catastrophe by sheer dumb luck.

740680103.text: You should try adding up those percentages and seeing just what the total is...

740680104.text: Don't mind that, just face the... Right, that chair is where the audience should be. You must look in that direction when saying the line...

740680105.text: You have to imagine someone sitting over there!
